title: Authentication vs Authorization with Active Directory
built: Created two standard domain users and one protected SMB folder, with read access granted through an AD security group and enforced by NTFS permissions.
problem: Successful sign-in establishes identity; group-based authorization limits which resources that identity can access.
objective: Prove both standard users can sign in while only the authorized group member can open the same protected folder.
outcome: Both standard users signed in to Windows. The group member listed the folder and read its file; the nonmember received Access Denied. The reader could not write. Group membership, permissions and share access were verified again after a controller restart.

tests.expected: Protected group read/execute; no direct user ACE
Signed-in reader lists the protected folder
Signed-in nonmember denied the same folder
Share, exact membership and ACL remain
tests.observed: Share present; same member and SDDL; directory services running

problems: Early client clock values differed from host capture timestamps; provenance retains the host time.
A controller restart interrupted the secure channel; domain connectivity was re-established before the final functional checks.
